title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All executive and non-executive Directors, officers and employees (including AASB 124 Key Management Personnel) and their associates, plus contractors, consultants, advisors and auditors. Baseline restriction is the Closed Period ban and the insider trading prohibition; no general pre-clearance requirement.

tiers.name: ELT and direct reports
tiers.description: Members of the Executive Leadership Team and Employees who report directly to the ELT; must obtain the CEO's prior written approval before trading in Securities at all times, not only during Closed Periods.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Executive and non-executive Directors; must obtain the Chairman's prior written approval before trading at all times (the Chairman must obtain approval from the Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee), and must notify the Company Secretary of trade details within 2 days.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions with Securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes

windows.end_anchor: opening of the market on the business day following release of the Company's half yearly accounts to the ASX
opening of the market on the business day following release of the Company's preliminary annual accounts to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other period to be a blackout period from time to time; the Company Secretary or CFO will notify Employees of the precise opening and closing dates, so it is not run as a confidential prohibition.

rules.detail: Named ban on transactions in Securities or any derivative thereof in associated products that limit the economic risk of unvested equity-incentive entitlements, expressly limited to executive and non-executive Directors.
rules.evidence: Executive and non-executive Directors are not permitted to enter into transactions with Securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.

rules.detail: Section 6's derivative/anti-hedging ban is expressed to apply only to executive and non-executive Directors; it is not extended to ELT or other Employees hedging unvested entitlements.

'Securities' is defined as Shares plus options, warrants, debentures and other securities on issue by the Company; a third-party OTC put or call is not within that definition, and the general trading/insider-trading/Closed Period provisions are keyed to 'Securities', so such an instrument over vested, unrestricted shares is not addressed outside the general law.
Anti-Hedging Policy bars Directors from any transaction (including via derivatives or associated products) limiting the economic risk of unvested equity-incentive entitlements.
rules.evidence: Executive and non-executive Directors are not permitted to enter into transactions with Securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.

rules.detail: The Anti-Hedging Policy (section 6) is confined to Directors; ELT and other Employees hedging unvested entitlements are not addressed.
No hedging restriction is stated for vested, unrestricted holdings for any tier.

Monetisation is not named; a forward sale or similar disposal of Securities is 'trading' for which Directors need the Chairman's prior written approval at all times, and it remains subject to the Closed Period ban absent an exceptional-circumstances approval.
rules.evidence: Directors must submit a request for approval in writing (which may be by email) to the Chairman before trading in the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation would be 'trading' requiring the CEO's prior written approval at all times, plus compliance with the Closed Period ban.
rules.evidence: At all times, members of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and all Employees who report directly to the ELT must submit a request for approval in writing (which may be by email) to the Chief Executive Officer before trading in the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: For rank-and-file Employees, no general pre-clearance is required; a disposal-type transaction is only barred during a Closed Period or while in possession of inside information.
rules.evidence: the Board has determined that Employees are prohibited from dealing in Company Securities during the following periods (Closed Periods).

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the 'Securities' definition or trading restrictions.
CFDs are not named and, like other third-party derivatives, fall outside the narrow 'Securities' definition (Shares, options, warrants, debentures on issue by the Company).

Entering into a margin lending arrangement is not itself restricted or made subject to clearance or Board notice; the Policy implicitly contemplates such arrangements by excluding a secured lender's forced sale from the trading restrictions altogether.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting security over Securities is not listed in the trading restrictions and is not made conditional on any notice to the Board; only the resulting forced sale on enforcement is expressly addressed, as Excluded Trading.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: The carve-out is drafted around 'a secured lender exercising their rights', with margin lending only the example given, so the scope extends to secured financing generally; no notice-to-Board condition is attached, unlike some peer policies.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: No short-term or speculative dealing restriction is stated anywhere in the Policy.

clearance.evidence: the Board has determined that Employees are prohibited from dealing in Company Securities during the following periods (Closed Periods).

At all times, members of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and all Employees who report directly to the ELT must submit a request for approval in writing (which may be by email) to the Chief Executive Officer before trading in the Company's Securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman (Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee for the Chairman's own trades)
clearance.evidence: Directors must submit a request for approval in writing (which may be by email) to the Chairman before trading in the Company's Securities. ... Executive and non-executive Directors must provide the Company Secretary with full details of any trading in the Company's Securities within two (2) days of the transaction.

exceptions.evidence: transfer of Securities in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Employee is a beneficiary, but the Employee has no control or influence over the investment decisions made by the superannuation fund or saving scheme.

an investment in, or trading units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

where an Employee is a trustee, trading in Securities by that trust provided the Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Closed Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Employee.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.

exceptions.approver: Board (approves the plan determining timing and structure)
exceptions.evidence: trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend, or distribution investment plan (DRP) and an equal access buy-back.
a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Closed Period and where the Employee could not reasonably have been able to exercise at a time when free to do so.

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... the trading plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

exceptions.approver: Chief Executive Officer (non-executive Directors, for the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship which means an Employee has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the Securities.

exceptions.approver: Chief Executive Officer (non-executive Directors, for the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: if the Employee is required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings to transfer or sell the Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for the Employee to do so.
a situation determined by the Chairman or, in the case of the Chairman, the non-executive Directors, to be an exceptional circumstance.

exemption_authority: Chief Executive Officer for a general Employee's exceptional-circumstances sale during a Closed Period; Chairman (or all non-executive Directors, for the Chairman's own exceptional-circumstances request) for the same. There is no exemption authority over, or notice condition on, entering a secured financing arrangement or the section 6 anti-hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: always-on pre-clearance for Directors and ELT
bespoke_clauses.clause: At all times, members of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and all Employees who report directly to the ELT must submit a request for approval in writing ... to the Chief Executive Officer before trading ... Directors must submit a request for approval in writing ... to the Chairman before trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary Employees, a Director or ELT member needs written pre-approval before every trade at any time of year, so each leg of a collar (entry, roll or unwind) requires case-by-case Chairman/CEO sign-off regardless of the Closed Period calendar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Executive and non-executive Directors are not permitted to enter into transactions with Securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivative/hedging ban binds only Directors and only over unvested equity-incentive entitlements; it does not reach a Director's vested, unrestricted shares or restrict ELT/other Employees at all, so a funded collar over vested shares is not caught by this clause for any tier.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no notice condition on secured lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This Policy, unlike some peers, does not require prior notice to the Board before entering a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, and a lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the trading restrictions outright, reducing procedural friction for a bank-secured loan leg.

bespoke_clauses.topic: narrow Securities definition excludes third-party derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include Shares as well as options, warrants, debentures, and any other security on issue from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because 'Securities' is limited to instruments issued by the Company, a bank-written OTC put/call or CFD referencing SVR shares arguably falls outside the Policy's dealing, insider-trading and Closed Period machinery altogether, other than the general legal insider-trading prohibition.

summary: A funded collar appears readily achievable under this policy, especially over vested, unrestricted shares. 'Securities' is defined narrowly as Company-issued shares, options, warrants and debentures, so a third-party OTC put and call arguably sit outside the Policy's dealing and insider-trading machinery, and the section 6 anti-hedging ban binds only executive and non-executive Directors and only over unvested equity-incentive entitlements, not vested shares and not other Employees. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is likewise unrestricted: the Policy simply excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from its trading rules, with no prior Board notice required. The principal constraint is procedural: Directors and ELT/direct reports must obtain written pre-approval (Chairman or CEO respectively) before every trade at all times, Directors must notify the Company Secretary within two days, and all Employees remain barred from dealing during the two Closed Periods or while possessing inside information (subject to a hardship/court-order/exceptional-circumstances sale process). There is no minimum holding period or short-selling ban to constrain collar tenor.
